nodes.summary: A quantifier-free formula of the language of groups in conjunctive normal form is coded as a finite list of clauses, each clause a finite list of literals. A literal is a pair $(b, w)$ of a Boolean $b$ and a group word $w$; it stands for the equation $w = 1$ when $b$ is true and for the inequation $w \ne 1$ when $b$ is false. nodes.title: Truth of a formula in conjunctive normal form

nodes.summary: A prenex sentence $(q, \varphi)$ holds in a group $G$ when the formula with quantifier prefix $q$ and matrix $\varphi$, whose quantifiers bind the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ in order, is true in $G$ under the assignment that gives every variable the value $1$; thus the variables not bound by $q$ are read as $1$.

nodes.title: Truth of a prenex formula

nodes.summary: For every torsion-free word-hyperbolic group $G$ (every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ has infinite order), the set of prenex sentences of the language of groups that hold in $G$ is computable, that is, some algorithm decides for each prenex sentence whether it holds in $G$.
nodes.title: Torsion-free hyperbolic groups have decidable elementary theory

nodes.summary: The proposition stating Kourovka Problem 16.71 (A. G. Myasnikov, O. G. Kharlampovich): for every torsion-free word-hyperbolic group $G$ (every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ has infinite order), the set of prenex sentences of the language of groups that hold in $G$ is computable, that is, some algorithm decides for each prenex sentence whether it holds in $G$.
nodes.title: Decidability of the elementary theory of torsion-free hyperbolic groups

nodes.summary: A group word in the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ is coded as a finite list of letters $(i, b)$, where $i$ is a natural number and $b$ is a Boolean: the letter $(i, \mathrm{true})$ stands for $x_i$ and the letter $(i, \mathrm{false})$ for $x_i^{-1}$. The word is read as the product of its letters in order, an element of the free group on $x_0, x_1, \dots$.
